title: 3-Read Friday #92
author: Craig Barton
summary: Issue 92 of 3-Read Friday is dominated by AI tools for teachers. Barton first flags Carl Hendrick's hands-on concerns about ChatGPT's new dedicated teacher tool, noting Hendrick 'has some concerns' after experimenting with it. He then highlights Dario Emanuele's work training Google's Gemini 3.0 model to plan lessons through 'atomisation,' revealing his own excitement about Gemini 3.0 and promising to share his own experiments with it in coming weeks -- a rare moment of Barton signalling his own AI adoption plans rather than just curating others'. The issue closes on a lighter, purely pedagogical note with Tom Manners's deep dive into the ambiguity of the word 'times' in maths instruction, which Barton flags as 'one for the maths geeks.' The issue's throughline is Barton actively tracking the frontier of AI-assisted lesson planning tools even as he curates a grounded classroom-language piece alongside it.
points: Barton flags that Hendrick has hands-on 'concerns' about ChatGPT's new dedicated teacher tool, signalling skepticism about a major AI vendor's move into classroom-specific products.

Barton discloses his own enthusiasm for Google's Gemini 3.0 model and promises to share his own experiments with it -- an unusually personal editorial aside that shows him actively adopting the same AI tooling Emanuele writes about.

Emanuele's atomisation-with-AI lesson-planning work is framed as 'fascinating' precisely because he has made his prompts and resources public, inviting readers to replicate the process rather than just read about it.
The Tom Manners piece on the word 'times' is explicitly framed as a lighter, vocabulary-consistency post for 'maths geeks,' contrasting with the two AI-tool pieces that dominate the issue.
quotes: Carl has been playing around with ChatGPT’s brand-new teacher tool… and he has some concerns!
Like Dario, I have been very impressed by Google’s latest model, Gemini 3.0. I will share some of my experiments in the coming weeks.
In the meantime, dive into Dario's fascinating work training Gemini to plan lessons. He has even shared his resources so you can try!
One for the maths geeks to finish this week. Tom takes a deep dive into the meaning - or meanings - of the word “times”, and why consistency of vocabulary matters.
